questions.q: What does 'materialization' actually control in dbt?
options: How a model's SQL gets built in the warehouse — as a view, table, incremental table, or ephemeral CTE
What columns a model is allowed to select
Which warehouse a model is allowed to run against
Whether a model can use ref() or not
questions.explain: Materialization is purely about how a model gets physically (or not) built — the SQL logic itself doesn't change.

questions.q: What happens with a view materialization?
options: No data is stored — the underlying query re-runs every time something selects from it
Data is stored once and never updated again
Only new rows are processed on each run
It's inlined directly into other models as a CTE
questions.explain: A view materialization creates a database view: no stored data, the query re-executes on every read.

questions.q: What is unique about an ephemeral materialization compared to the other three?
options: It never becomes an actual database object — it's inlined as a CTE wherever it's referenced
It always must be a table, never a view
It's the only materialization that supports ref()
It processes only new or changed rows
questions.explain: Ephemeral models don't exist as views or tables in the database at all — they get compiled directly into a CTE inside whatever model references them.

questions.q: According to this lesson, why do staging models commonly default to view while marts models default to table?
options: Staging's cleanup is cheap to re-run, while marts' joins/aggregation are expensive, so storing marts results avoids repeated cost
Staging models are not allowed to be tables under any circumstances
Marts models can never be views due to a technical limitation
There is no real reason — it's purely arbitrary convention
questions.explain: The lesson frames the choice around cost and query frequency: cheap, rarely-queried staging logic suits a view; expensive, frequently-queried marts logic suits a stored table.

questions.q: How do you override a model's materialization at the file level, rather than the project level?
options: {{ config(materialized='table') }} inside the model's .sql file
Renaming the file to end in .table.sql
Materializations cannot be set per-file, only project-wide
Adding a comment at the top of the SQL file
questions.explain: A config() call inside the model file itself overrides whatever default is set in dbt_project.yml.
